Able to break or be broken.

examples.text: The accident was also one of several since Clapham […] that demonstrated the role of breakable windows in the death toll. RSSB research would later confirm and reinforce the need for laminated glass to protect passengers and increase survivability.

glosses: Fragile.

examples.text: Next Christmas she sent us bisque dolls, very lovely but too breakable to hug; we could not even kiss them but they cracked.

glosses: Something that is (easily) breakable.

examples.text: We had to wrap all the breakables before the movers arrived.

She was, she wrote, “impatient and absent-minded, prone to drop things intentionally or through clumsiness, even breakables like dishes and love affairs; a woman who is perennially on the move, changing jobs and homes at the drop of a hat and inventing reasons afterward while she is packing; a person who runs away as soon as she gets nervous, long before she smells danger.”

glosses: A set of customized hardware that is part of a drum kit. Breakables typically consist of: the drummer's cymbals including high-hats, the snare drum, the kick pedal and the drummer's stool.
Inflexible; liable to break, snap, or shatter easily under stress, pressure, or impact; crackly.

examples.text: Cast iron is much more brittle than forged iron.
A diamond is hard but brittle.

'Do you suppose our convent, and I too,
 Are insufficient, then, to pray for you?
 Thomas, that joke's not good. Your faith is brittle.

glosses: Not physically tough or tenacious; apt to break or crumble when bending.

examples.text: Shortbread is my favorite cold pastry, yet being so brittle it crumbles easily, and a lot goes to waste.

glosses: Tending to fracture in a conchoidal way; capable of being knapped or flaked.
Emotionally fragile, easily offended.

examples.text: What a brittle personality! A little misunderstanding and he's an emotional wreck.

glosses: Poorly error- or fault-tolerant; having little in the way of redundancy or defense in depth; susceptible to catastrophic failure in the event of a relatively-minor malfunction or deviance.
Characterized by dramatic swings in blood sugar level.
A confection of caramelized sugar and nuts.

examples.text: As a child, my favorite candy was peanut brittle.

glosses: Anything resembling this confection, such as flapjack, a cereal bar, etc.
To become brittle.

examples.text: The project is based on a similar project, the Class project, which was started by the University of Cornell several years ago under the leadership of Stuart Lynn to preserve brittling old books.
Her heart fluttered, then stilled when May snapped the image away and her voice brittled.

glosses: To gut.

examples.text: Not being versed in the terms of English venery, he asked Abbot Ulfketyl what brittling of a deer might mean; and being informed that it was that operation on the carcass of a stag which his countrymen called eventrer, and Highland gillies now “gralloching”[.]

glosses: Easily broken into small fragments, crumbled, or reduced to powder.

examples.text: Spiders had woven their vague trapezes between the friable heads of dead peonies in enormous glass jars streaked with tide marks where the water had evaporated long ago.
This light, friable type of material offered excellent insulation against both desert heat and also the cold of darkness during the winter.

glosses: Of soil, loose and large-grained in consistency.

examples.text: So while two men under his directions were digging the grave with sticks in the friable granitic soil, he superintended the costume of the other actors in the drama.

glosses: Of a poison, likely to crumble and become airborne, thus becoming a health risk.

examples.text: It is when asbestos-containing products are friable that hazardous asbestos fibers are likely to be released and sent airborne.

glosses: Of a number: smooth, that factors completely into small prime numbers.
Easily broken, not sturdy; of delicate material.

examples.text: She caught the fragile vase before it could shatter on the floor.
The chemist synthesizes a fragile molecule.

glosses: Readily disrupted or destroyed.

examples.text: The UN tries to maintain the fragile peace process in the region.

glosses: Feeling weak or easily disturbed as a result of illness.
Thin-skinned or oversensitive.

examples.text: He is a very fragile person and gets easily depressed.
